title: coord.py serve and its client send operator tokens over plain http to a non-loopback host with no warning
goal: SP-rsmmwzr2 review G7 (ST-rk5ks4pf): serve --bind on a non-loopback host starts with only its 'serving http://...' line, and send() puts the bearer token on any http:// url, though the kb's RFC 6750 fact (kb/public/mcp/authorization.md) says the token needs TLS; only the docstring and kb/_self/tools.md mention a TLS front end. Both sides warn on stderr (or refuse without an explicit flag) for plain http to a host that is not loopback.

run:
import sys
t=open('_tools/coord.py',encoding='utf-8').read()
ok='is_loopback' in t
print('coord.py tests a host for loopback before plain http:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

repro_reason: binding a non-loopback address or sending to a remote host in a repro would expose a server on, or reach out of, the host's network; the repro reads coord.py for a loopback test on the plain-http path instead
